capabilities.target: private repositories owned by the user
pull request on the public repository

inputs.source: User's direct chat prompt in the desktop client
Issue content in the public GitHub repository, which any GitHub user can author

controls.name: Per-tool-call client approval prompt
controls.decay_rationale: The approver reviews a collapsed, model-generated summary rather than the raw destination and payload (approval_review_mode: model_summary), and the runtime notes state users approve many calls per session. A more persuasive model, or simply higher call volume, degrades this gate (ASI09, SAFE-T1403 consent-fatigue).

controls.name: Repository-scoped fine-grained PAT (public repo only)
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. The declared token has repo scope across every repository the user owns. A fine-grained PAT limited to the single public repository being worked on would make cap.read_private_repo unreachable by this agent regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Raw-action approval review for sensitive sequences
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Showing the approver the full, uncollapsed destination repository and diff (rather than a collapsed model summary) for any create_pull_request call that follows a private-repo read would remove reliance on the model's framing of its own action.

controls.name: Pinned MCP server image digest
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. The docker run command pulls ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server with no tag or digest, so docker will fetch whatever the tag currently resolves to. Pinning to a verified digest would prevent a silently altered upstream image from redefining tool behavior.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): planted public issue drives a private-repo read and exfiltration via a public pull request

attack_path.note: Attacker-authored issue in the public repo enters the agent's context as part of 'look at open issues'.
Agent follows injected instructions and reads confidential content from a private repo, reachable because the PAT is scoped broadly across all the user's repos.
Agent opens a pull request on the public repo containing or referencing the private content, visible to the issue's author and anyone else.

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric's credited floor for this path is moderate (critical minus two tiers for the approval gate). That classification already marks the gate partially_dependent for its model_summary review mode, but it does not separately capture the stated approval-fatigue condition (users approve many calls per session with collapsed arguments) or that this design reproduces a documented public incident in which exactly this GitHub MCP architecture allowed a planted issue to exfiltrate private repository content via a public pull request despite the same per-call human approval gate. Because the gate is known to have failed under these conditions in practice, residual is rated high rather than the computed floor of moderate.

forecast.watch_signal: Monitor for: the approval UI switching to a remembered/always-allow mode, approvals-per-session continuing to rise, the client model being upgraded, or the per-call prompt being disabled or narrowed. Any of these removes the only existing control on this path.

evidence.observation: Agent is wired to the official GitHub MCP server via docker with GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN; no tool allowlist, credential scoping, or egress restriction is declared beyond the token's own scope.
The personal access token has repo scope across every repository the user owns, public and private, so a task framed around the public repo can still reach private-repo reads.
Anyone on GitHub can open issues in the public repository, making issue content an untrusted (U) input that enters the agent's context alongside the trusted user request.

Approval is per tool call but arguments are collapsed by default and users approve many calls per session, matching the consent-fatigue pattern (SAFE-T1403) that is documented to have defeated this exact gate in a public incident.

recommendations.action: Scope the credential to a fine-grained PAT limited to the public repository in scope for this task, so cap.read_private_repo is unreachable by this agent at all.

Require raw_action approval review (full destination repo and diff visible, not a collapsed summary) specifically for any create_pull_request call that follows a private-repo read earlier in the same session.
Log and alert on any session where a private-repo read is followed by a write/egress action to a public-facing target.

findings.title: Unpinned GitHub MCP server image enables a future silent tool redefinition (ASI04 rug pull)

attack_path.note: Docker pulls ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server with no tag or digest pinned.

threat_refs.name: Publish Poisoned AI Artifacts: AI Agent Tools

forecast.watch_signal: Any change in the resolved image digest for ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server outside a reviewed release process, or removal of any future pinning control once added.

evidence.observation: The docker run command references ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server with no tag or digest, so the image resolved at pull time can change without the deploying team's review.

recommendations.action: Pin the MCP server to a specific, verified image digest and re-verify before each pull.
Monitor the published image's digest and alert on any change outside a reviewed release process.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted public-issue input can, via an unrestrained task-level credential and no structural containment, reach an irreversible, egress-capable capability (public PR creation) after reading confidential private-repo content. The only present control, a per-tool-call approval prompt, is a model_summary gate degraded by approval fatigue; the rubric's credited floor is moderate, but the design reproduces a documented public incident in which this exact gate failed, so residual is rated high. Forecast is critical: under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, or control_removal the one existing control is expected to fail outright, and separately, if the unpinned MCP server image is ever swapped (new_mcp_server), the same critical outcome follows through a different path. The single highest-leverage fix is scoping the GitHub credential to only the public repository in scope, which would sever the private-read path entirely.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided configuration and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No system prompt or orchestration source code was provided; autonomy step/runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) were not declared and are treated as null/uncapped, which is a conservative assumption stated here rather than confirmed.

Whether the GitHub MCP server image is actually unpinned at the registry level (versus pinned elsewhere outside the shown config) was not independently verified; confidence on finding f2 is accordingly low.
Peer identity verification and the exact behavior of the client's collapsed-argument approval UI were inferred from the runtime notes and were not independently tested.
